body:
Minor release: `@claude-flow/cli`, `claude-flow`, `ruflo` 3.62.0. Adds one MCP tool (`rure_cuda_launch_plan`). No leaf package changed, so no standalone publishes.

### Added

- **ruRE: CUDA launch plan** (ruflo-rure 0.6.0, ADR-501). New read-only MCP tool `rure_cuda_launch_plan` turns what `rure_analyze_cuda` found into a plan for measuring: per architecture and kernel, how many blocks and warps fit on one multiprocessor at each block size, which resource sets the limit (registers, shared memory, warps, block slots, barriers), the best block sizes and flags. Eight architectures have a table (`sm_70` to `sm_120`); any other gets no figure rather than a guess. It still parses and never runs: `includeHarness` only returns the text of a small CUDA program for you to build and run yourself. The occupancy model matches NVIDIA's `cuda_occupancy.h` on 1.77 million combinations and the CUDA driver on five real GPUs (ADR-501, ADR-500).

### Fixed

- `rure_analyze_cuda` reported the wrong architecture (`sm_5`) for a standalone `.cubin` built with CUDA 12 for `sm_70` to `sm_90`; the SM number sits in a different byte depending on the cubin's OS ABI. Cubins inside a fatbin or host binary were not affected.
- The worker daemon let a `maxConcurrent` or `workerTimeoutMs` saved in `daemon-state.json` override the same setting in `config.json`; an explicit value now wins (constructor, then config file, then saved state, then default) (#4462).
- Cancelling a headless worker now settles its execution and escalates to SIGKILL when the child ignores SIGTERM; the fallback timer no longer keeps the host alive, and a timed-out child no longer gets a second SIGTERM (#4463).

### Notes

- Plugins in this tree that changed: `ruflo-rure` 0.6.0, `ruflo-ai-team` 0.3.4, `ruflo-browser` 0.3.7 (doctor path from other working directories), `ruflo-x-gateway` 0.10.2. The x.ruv.io gateway itself (0.9.1) is a separate deployment.
- `@claude-flow/swarm` changes (#4456, #4457) are not a CLI dependency an
name: v3.62.0 — ruRE CUDA launch plan

Fixes from the community. Thanks to everyone who reported and sent them.

- **Safe text in charts and split headings** (#160, #169, thanks @jcastilla89 and @Pablolakotek): `charts.js` and the `Stage.split` fallback escape the text they insert, so a label or heading from user data can no longer inject markup.
- **No lost screenshots when two widths share a class** (#162, #165, thanks @nosawavey-spec and @ketpatil77).
- **Keyboard and accessible names** (#170, thanks @MrBinnacle): every control works from the keyboard and has an accessible name.
- **The italic faces load** (#161, fix from #166, thanks @nosawavey-spec and @ketpatil77): Boska, Erode and Sentient request their italic weight.
- **`edge-text` no longer fails ellipsised lines** (#156, thanks @shoctroper).
- **Inspect the production build** (#171, thanks @lilozzy): the Gate says so, and the inspector warns when it is looking at a dev server.
- **The redraw rule names its third reason** (#163, thanks @Tsury).
- CI also checks that every text file is clean UTF-8.

body:
This hotfix restores self-hosted Compose startup after the 0.9.4 update.

- **Restore dashboard readiness and edge startup** — bind the dashboard's Next.js
  server to `0.0.0.0` inside its container so the loopback healthcheck can reach it.
  Apply the same bind setting in the CLI-generated, reference self-hosted and
  from-source Compose environments. Published host ports retain their existing
  loopback defaults (#1461).
- **Test the complete customer upgrade** — gate image publication on upgrades from
  0.9.3 and the previous release using their published API, dashboard and edge
  images and CLI templates. Verify populated PostgreSQL and Redis storage, custom
  ports, preserved secrets, admin credentials and signed sessions, saved edge
  routing, dashboard-to-API access, cold
  restart and fresh installation. Probe both dashboard image architectures before
  publication; an API-only migration check no longer stands in for a stack upgrade.
- **Explain source rebuild prerequisites before a security refresh** — global and
  project advisory views use the same runtime-update preflight as the deployment
  action. Replayed or revisionless source images show their prerequisite and an
  **Open source redeploy** action instead of offering a refresh that will fail.
  Redeploy still uses the existing project deployment controls; source provenance,
  image pins and tenant authorization remain enforced (#1462).
- **Include the packaged-worker image correction** — source builds of managed
  workers require Git checkout metadata. Bundled Dockerfiles in the released API
  no longer trigger a development worker build.

### Recovery from 0.9.4

Run `openship update` after 0.9.5 is published. The update recreates the API,
dashboard and edge through the normal pipeline and preserves existing database,
Redis and application storage. For a temporary recovery on 0.9.4, set
`HOSTNAME: "0.0.0.0"` in the dashboard service's Compose `environment` and run
`docker compose up -d` with that in

## What's in v0.10.2


Codewhale v0.10.2 adds an animated pet view (`/pet on`), a live Terminal work
dock, per-chat composer colors (`/color`) and a one-time note on the first
start after an update that says what changed. It closes three session
data-loss paths and a `codewhale web` session leak; adds the default Runtime
daemon socket locations to the sandbox deny-list; holds a `curl` or `wget` that uploads a
credential; refuses shell commands containing invisible Unicode; keeps the
Linux sandbox working when a hidden credential directory is a symlink; and
reduces idle TUI redraw work. `/undo` takes back a whole
request, including long and multiline prompts. `exec --auto` explains its
Full Access default, honors an explicitly stricter sandbox, and saves
tool-enabled runs and their failure receipts. Local runtimes appear during
onboarding, `/diff` works outside a Git repository, DeepSeek's Responses route
no longer rejects replayed tool history, and contributor fixes improve token
accounting, relay model lists, localized replies and Windows launcher
guidance. Delegated work continues without model-invented turn or time caps,
and independent workflow steps can continue after another child fails.

## Install

### Recommended — official GitHub release

New macOS/Linux install (checksummed binaries from this release):

```bash
curl -fsSL https://codewhale.net/install.sh | CODEWHALE_VERSION="v0.10.2" sh
```

- **Cheaper** than vector RAG: for both index and query.
- **Faster**: trees are created from layout stats.
- **Unified** SDK: vectorless RAG. **Local** or **cloud**, for index and chat.
- Runs on your **Claude subscription**.

Index, to chat, to agent integration, one client.
Local mode needs no server, no vector DB, no PageIndex API key.

```python
client = PageIndexClient()
client.submit_document("report.pdf")
client.chat("What does the report conclude?")
```

## Highlights

- **Flash engine**: the local default (`mode="standard"` keeps the classic LLM pipeline). Embedded bookmarks are consumed when trustworthy, and tree optimization is on by default — `optimize="merge"` for the deterministic LLM-free pass, `"full"` (default) adds LLM expand, which runs a wave of nodes concurrently instead of one round-trip at a time.
- **One complete surface, local and cloud**: `PageIndexLocalClient(storage_path=...)` is the same client as cloud — submit, tree, page content, chat, and agent tools all present in both modes, so code moves between them unchanged.
- **Cloud documents, your own model**: `api_key` decides where your documents live; a configured chat model decides who answers — and the two combine. `PageIndexClient(api_key="pi-...", chat_model="openai/gpt-5.2")` runs the same in-process document-QA engine over the live cloud tool set. Page content flows through your process to your provider on your credentials; `doc_id` targets at the prompt level; `enable_citations` stays with the managed chat.
- **Agent integration**: the cloud MCP tool contract, in-process — `client.agent_tools()` (plain functions), `as_openai_tools()`, `as_anthropic_tools()`, `as_claude_mcp()`, plus one-call `openai_agent_config()` / `anthropic_runner_config()` / `claude_agent_config()` bundles and `agent_instructions()` for the system prompt. Cloud clients get the live server tool set over the MCP bridge (read-only endpoint by default); local clients get the in-process subset with the same schemas

**Two releases today!** Check out the [v1.4.238 release notes](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases/tag/v1.4.238) too. That release brought shared unsaved edits across workspaces, richer agent chats and remote account setup, a more capable browser, and smoother phone controls.

## Your workspace, working together 🐳

Set up agent skills in one click, keep browser sessions separate between projects, and move more easily between chat and terminal. This release also strengthens the essentials: shared files stay in sync, SSH sessions recover more reliably, and phone interactions feel more predictable.

## The short version

- **Skills, ready wherever you work:** Install Orca’s skills in one click from setup screens, and install or update them on paired servers and SSH hosts with Orca’s own installer.

- **More fluid agent conversations:** Split into a fresh chat beside your current one, continue with a terminal agent from the pane header, and keep queued messages and multiple image attachments intact.

Patch release: `@claude-flow/cli`, `claude-flow`, `ruflo` 3.61.1. No leaf package changed, so no standalone publishes.

### Added

- `ruflo-console` 0.48.0 (ADR-499): the ruRE page can read a folder outside the project that you allow. New plugin option `rureFolders` (`name=/absolute/folder` pairs); a sample then names it as `@name/sub/file`. Absolute paths, `..` and odd characters in a sample are still refused; the folder and every part below it must not be a link; and changing the option is an install-class write that always asks you first (Claude's console tools can only propose it at the full control level). ruRE still only parses. This is the version that `ruflo tui` ships, which is why it needs a CLI release.

### Notes

- CI: plugin pull requests now fail unless the plugin's `plugin.json` version rises when shipped files change (#4447).
- `@claude-flow/plugins` (#4451, registry caches no longer re-run a surviving plugin's `register*` methods) is not a CLI dependency and is not part of this release.

_Automated prerelease from `develop` — **Server** v3.5.0._


### Fixed

- **parse**: RAR4 and RAR5 archives extracted nothing since #2440, silently and on every platform: the move of the Tika code into the parse node left `RarSevenZipParser` behind in the unbuilt `packages/tika`, so `ConfigBuilder` replaced Tika's RAR parser with a class that was not on the classpath. The class now lives in the parse node library, the swap checks that the class resolves before it removes Tika's own parser, and a RAR5 archive yields its member text again (#2678)
- **server**: a Linux task running parse beside a node that imports torch died at start with SIGSEGV in libstdc++: the jar's prebuilt `lib7-Zip-JBinding.so` carries a statically linked libstdc++ whose GNU-unique locale ids collided with the system runtime's. The engine now claims the system libstdc++ at startup, before any JNI library can (#2676, #2720)

The parse node now extracts the library itself, reuses a complete copy and publishes a new one only by an atomic rename (#2790)

Minor release: `@claude-flow/cli`, `claude-flow`, `ruflo` 3.61.0. Adds one MCP tool (`rure_analyze_cuda`). No leaf package changed, so no standalone publishes.

### Added

- **ruRE: CUDA static analysis** (ruflo-rure 0.5.0, plugin ADR-0006). New read-only MCP tool `rure_analyze_cuda` reads the GPU code inside a CUDA fatbin, cubin or PTX file: fatbin entries (PTX or cubin, target architecture, LZ4/zstd compression), each kernel with register count, code size and constant/shared/local memory, and PTX version, target and kernel names. It parses only; nothing is executed, and strings taken from the file pass the AIDefence gate. Checked against real nvcc 12.8 and 13.0 output. Not included: SASS decoding, `cuobjdump` shell-out. zstd entries need Node 22.15+.
- `ruflo-console` 0.47.0: a CUDA row on the ruRE page, DETECT routes for `.cubin`, `.fatbin` and `.ptx`, and a hint on a native binary that holds a CUDA fatbin (ADR-495..497). The ruRE page refuses a sample that is a symlink, wraps long lists, and shows Claude a structured `rure` block in `console_state`.
- `ruflo-mods` 0.7.0: opt-in `rureOffer` (off by default, ADR-498) adds one line under an answer when the model touched a binary, library, `.asar` or CUDA file, saying ruRE can inspect it without running it. Offer only; the mods plugin is not part of the CLI tarball.

### Fixed

- Dependency audit: `zod` 4.6.7 in `ruflo-graph-intelligence` and `@claude-flow/browser` (GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5). Nested zod 3 copies stay under two time-boxed accepted findings that expire 2026-11-23 (#4442, #4444).
name: v3.61.0 — ruRE reads CUDA (rure_analyze_cuda)

# HyperFrames v0.8.191

Released on 2026-10-24.

A deleted layer that a script still looks up now stays hidden instead of coming back, and a script that throws no longer blocks a render. Preview loads only the clips due next, so it holds up on slow links.

## Features

- **Studio:** Motion blur panel with Off / Subtle / Strong ([ffc327b44](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/ffc327b44c548576bb40be2eef14bc04d7694d6f), [#6112](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/6112)).

## Keep agent work in view while you work elsewhere

- **Keep agent work in view while you work elsewhere.** Desktop users can pop the computer view and floating browser into their own windows above other apps, and browser full screen now fills the display.
- **Dictate messages and use workspace commands again.** On macOS and Windows, dictation shows your words as you speak, stops when you click the mic again, and keeps words across pauses. On OpenCode v2, `/` lists workspace commands and skills, and picking one runs it.
- **Follow Workbot's browser work and longer tasks.** Workbot shows browser activity live and links to pages it opened. Background tasks can pass files and read just the part they need, while longer scripts and documents can finish without a cut-off reply being mistaken for completed work.
- **Invitations and connections take clearer paths.** Invited teammates can join their workspace during sign-in, invitation emails explain who invited them and where to get help, and completed MCP sign-ins no longer appear to fail. Teams messages and Outlook meeting invitations now wait for your confirmation.
- **For admins: organization and billing details are clearer.** Compact organization rows, recent organizations, and week-over-week summaries make admin pages easier to scan. The Free plan covers up to five users, and pending invitations count until they expire.
- **For self-hosters: web access and standalone installs are more predictable.** `openwork-server web` answers only its own host names unless you add proxy names with `--allowed-hosts`. Standalone server and bootstrap installs require Node.js 24.x (24.22.1 or newer), and the bootstrap installer downloads a supported runtime when needed.

body:
# Stop observer reasoning from consuming the output budget

Observer requests to OpenRouter, the cmem.ai gateway, and OpenAI-compatible endpoints now disable reasoning by default, so reasoning tokens no longer fill the output budget and leave a session with zero observations.

- An empty reply with finish_reason=length is logged and retried once with reasoning forced off. That retry counts against the existing paid-send budget and is bounded by the per-attempt timeout.
- Billed usage keeps the retry's prompt size and adds completion tokens and cost from both attempts.
- Health status names the active OpenRouter credential, including a custom OPENROUTER_BASE_URL.
- OpenAI "Unsupported parameter" responses drop the reasoning field and remember the endpoint. Mandatory-reasoning and invalid-effort refusals are left in place.
- Empty replies that finish with stop stay accepted.

Ships the observer repair from #5029.
name: v15.0.2 — Stop observer reasoning from consuming the output budget

## What's Changed

### Features
- Add support for LiteLLM-compatible kwargs.
- Implement platform application search in CLI.
- Highlight action picker search in CLI.
- Trace conversation routes and public replies in flow.
- Select organization during login in CLI.
- Add offline jev routing and guardrail evaluation runner.
- Run integration app actions directly with call: tool.
- Promote AgentExecutor out of experimental status.
- Add Azure DocumentDB vector search integration.
- Add read-only notebook text loader and standard-library jsonl loader.
- Ensure crewAI eval keeps the evaluation's full data in the project.
- Enable crewAI eval to run the crew itself for verdict from one command.
- Allow crewAI eval to export evaluations as files.

### Bug Fixes
- Fix platform integration token derivation from login.
- Resolve logging issues by preserving JSON logs on serialization errors.
- Skip non-UTF-8 cached skill metadata.
- Fix tool actions to honor failure policies and get fresh usage budgets per kickoff.
- Prevent private memories without a source from leaking to every recall.
- Fix memory record retrieval order in LanceDBStorage.
- Restore task description when replanning fails.
- Stop agents from repeating the same tool call.
- Escape scope and id values in LanceDB filters.

### Documentation
- Update broken links in crewAI examples and observability guides.
- Fix dead links in tools documentation.

### Refactoring
- Refactor context compaction to be a BaseLLM capability.

## Contributors

@Akaliup, @Arxsher, @Copilot, @D41910, @LindseyZ1205, @RaycarlLei, @Rohitkanithi, @Sakura-798, @Vidit-Ostwal, @Wilson0511, @Winoren, @abdullahajaz14, @bballhaus, @gabemilani, @iris-clawd, @joaomdmoura, @leom1919, @lorenzejay, @marcreniel, @mattatcha, @reubenjrouse, @rohitkanithi, @sandeepsnairms, @stepchanges, @subhashpolisetti, @theCyberTech, @vatsalyd

Minor release: `@claude-flow/cli`, `claude-flow`, `ruflo` 3.60.0, with `@claude-flow/hooks` 3.0.2 and `@claude-flow/mcp` 3.1.2 published standalone. Backward-compatible additions (six new reverse-engineering MCP tools, a ruRE page in the console) plus security and correctness fixes. The 3.59.x patch releases are not itemised here; this lists what changed since 3.59.17.

### Added

- **ruRE: static reverse engineering** (ruflo-rure 0.4.2, ADR-0001..0005 of the plugin). Six read-only MCP tools — `rure_extract_asar`, `rure_analyze_js_app`, `rure_find_feature`, `rure_analyze_binary` (ELF, PE, Mach-O), `rure_analyze_dotnet` (metadata only) and `rure_analyze_evm` (bytecode inventory) — that parse a file and never run it. Every string taken from the analyzed file passes the AIDefence gate; results say `screened: false` when the scanner is unavailable. New dependency: `@electron/asar`. Known gaps: EVM and P/Invoke handling validated on built fixtures only; the `.asar` scratch folder is not cleaned up; the tools read any path the process can read.
- `ruflo-console` 0.45.0: a **ruRE** page in the TOOLS group (ADR-494) with a row per tool, a project-relative `sample` field, and results cleaned of terminal escapes. The tools are needed in the CLI: on 3.59.17 and older the rows say to update.
- `agentic-qe-fleet` marketplace pin moved to v3.15.12 (#4419).

### Fixed

- **Security**: `agentbbs` accepted `..` in a room id, letting a room log path escape `.agentbbs` (#4416).

body:
- **Cheaper** than vector RAG: for both index and query.
- **Faster**: trees are created from layout stats.
- **Unified** SDK: vectorless RAG. **Local** or **cloud**, for index and chat.
- Runs on your **Claude subscription**.

Index, to chat, to agent integration, one client.
Local mode needs no server, no vector DB, no PageIndex API key.

```python
client = PageIndexClient()
client.submit_document("report.pdf")
client.chat("What does the report conclude?")
```

## Highlights

- **Flash engine**: the local default (`mode="standard"` keeps the classic LLM pipeline). Embedded bookmarks are consumed when trustworthy, and tree optimization is on by default — `optimize="merge"` for the deterministic LLM-free pass, `"full"` (default) adds LLM expand, which runs a wave of nodes concurrently instead of one round-trip at a time.
- **One complete surface, local and cloud**: `PageIndexLocalClient(storage_path=...)` is the same client as cloud — submit, tree, page content, chat, and agent tools all present in both modes, so code moves between them unchanged.
- **Cloud documents, your own model**: `api_key` decides where your documents live; a configured chat model decides who answers — and the two combine. `PageIndexClient(api_key="pi-...", chat_model="openai/gpt-5.2")` runs the same in-process document-QA engine over the live cloud tool set. Page content flows through your process to your provider on your credentials; `doc_id` targets at the prompt level; `enable_citations` stays with the managed chat.
- **Agent integration**: the cloud MCP tool contract, in-process — `client.agent_tools()` (plain functions), `as_openai_tools()`, `as_anthropic_tools()`, `as_claude_mcp()`, plus one-call `openai_agent_config()` / `anthropic_runner_config()` / `claude_agent_config()` bundles and `agent_instructions()` for the system prompt. Cloud clients get the live server tool set over the MCP bridge (read-only endpoint by default); local clients get the in-process subset with the same schemas

## Behavior changes
- JS page errors now log under a new `page_error` scope at WARN (silence with `--log-filter`).
- Each top-level page now has its own session history; a second page no longer shows up in the first page's back/forward.
- `--block-private-networks` now blocks more non-routable ranges (CGNAT, benchmarking, multicast, reserved, NAT64).
- `no-cors` fetches with a non-safelisted method are now rejected.
- An unreadable `--http-cache-dir` database is now discarded instead of exiting.
- Console values written to the log are now escaped and capped.

## New Web APIs
- Web Crypto: Ed25519, X25519, ECDSA, RSA-PSS, RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5, `wrapKey`/`unwrapKey` + AES-KW; EC and RSA-OAEP import/export
- WebCodecs, `OfflineAudioContext`, WebVTT improvements
- XML document parsing
- `setRangeText()` on `<input>` and `<textarea>`; `textarea.textLength`
- `HTMLProgressElement` `value`/`max`/`position`; `HTMLOptionElement.index`; missing table APIs
- `document.hasFocus()`; `window.outerWidth/outerHeight/screenX/screenY/screenLeft/screenTop`
- `:nth-child(An+B of S)` and `:nth-last-child(An+B of S)`
- `PermissionStatus` is now an `EventTarget`; `DOMException` is now structured-cloneable; `ImageData` overload
- Missing global event handlers added to `window`, `document` and `body`

- Element widths are now resolved relative to their parent (block, inline, floats, %, min/max-width, basic flex)

- 从旧版升级：把"帮我更新 Agent Reach"那句话发给你的 AI 就行。你的密钥和设置都保留，旧版程序会自动删掉。
- 加一个平台只要说一句，需要的软件都会自动装好，不需要管理员密码；你只需要登录或者填一个 Key。
- 小红书、推特这类要登录的平台，改用 Agent Reach 自己的专用浏览器，不弹窗、不占用你的浏览器；多个 AI 可以同时查。
- RSS 订阅和 Exa 全网搜索合并进了"网页"。以后有新版本，AI 会用大白话告诉你改了什么，你同意了才更新。

English:

- Upgrading from an older version: just send your AI the "update Agent Reach" sentence. Your keys and settings are kept, and the old program is removed for you.
- Adding a platform takes one sentence. Everything it needs is installed for you, with no admin password; you only log in or enter a key.
- Platforms that need a login, such as Xiaohongshu and X, now use Agent Reach's own browser in the background, never yours, and several AIs can search at once.
- RSS and Exa search are now part of "web". When a new version is out, your AI tells you in plain words what changed and updates only if you say yes.

1.6 is a rebuild. Agents call one command, `agent-reach`; everything Agent Reach installs or stores lives under `~/.agent-reach/`.
1.6 是重构版本：Agent 只调一个命令 `agent-reach`，Agent Reach 装的、存的东西全部在 `~/.agent-reach/` 下。

中文（技术细节）：
- 本版发布前已真实测通 28/40 个动作；以下未在发布机上测通，经维护者批准随本版发布：Reddit（测试网络被拦）、Instagram（限流）、B站字幕、LinkedIn、雪球热帖热股（未登录）、小宇宙（未配 Key）。
- 修复未登录 gh 阻断公开 API、公开行情触发浏览器、错误认证提示和未登记缓存清理；临时音频/字幕保存在 Reach 内。BOSS 站内搜索优先官方 OpenCLI，JD 上游适配故障单列；PR 与发版均检查真实验收和待验状态。
- CLI 对已声明的公开搜索/阅读先复用网页工具，成功后不准备浏览器；结果标注来源和内容范围，站内路径明确要求认证时才提示登录。可指定后端保留原有站内能力。
- 浏览器渠道共用一份登录，闲置十分钟自动关闭，下次使用自动打开。
- 添加渠道自动准备工具；删除时只清理该网站的登录。默认平台也能去掉，去掉后更新不会再加回来。
- 更新时，有已测版本的工具保持在已测版本，其他工具用兼容范围内的最新版。

Dify 1.18.0 brings **Agents that route workflows**, **portable app packages**, **deeper visibility into nested workflow runs**, and the opt-in **Agent Knowledge Base** experience. OpenAPI and the new difyctl expand how you build and manage apps from the command line.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Read the upgrade guide below before deploying.** Upgrade the API, workers, Agent Backend, and Agent runtime images together. Local Agent sandboxes require a non-empty authentication token, and Agent Backend uses a new run protocol. Source installations require Python 3.13. Install the new difyctl client and sign in again. Preserve your existing `PASSWORD_PEPPER` configuration.

### Release highlights

#### Agents that choose the next step

Let an Agent decide which workflow branch to take. Enable **Output Routes**, give each route a selection condition, and connect it to the next step—such as resolving a request directly or handing it to a specialist. The read-only `switch` output exposes the chosen route. (#42599)

![Agent Output Routes with Resolve directly and Escalate to team branches](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/30480ac3-d53e-4522-b1c5-95eb1d9ac9f2)

*Output Routes configuration with two branches in the workflow editor.*

Plain Agent v2 nodes also stream text as it is generated. Structured results, routed results, and nodes using default-value error handling remain buffered. (#43986)

#### Portable apps in one package

Move an app with its supported resources in a single **`.ifpkg` package**. Workflow and Chatflow packages carry inline Agents, Skills, and their files; imports recreate those resources in the destination workspace and remap references. File and URL imports support both packages and YAML, and explicit YAML export remains available. (#42066, #42579, #42626, #42863)

body:
- **Unified** SDK: vectorless RAG. **Local** or **cloud**. Index or chat.
- **Faster**: trees are created from layout stats.
- **Cheaper** than **vector index**: LLMs only write node summaries.
- Runs on your **Claude subscription**.

Index, to chat, to agent integration, one client.
Local mode needs no server, no vector DB, no PageIndex API key.

```python
client = PageIndexClient()
client.submit_document("report.pdf")
client.chat("What does the report conclude?")
```

## Highlights

- **Flash engine**: the local default (`mode="standard"` keeps the classic LLM pipeline). Embedded bookmarks are consumed when trustworthy, and tree optimization is on by default — `optimize="merge"` for the deterministic LLM-free pass, `"full"` (default) adds LLM expand, which runs a wave of nodes concurrently instead of one round-trip at a time.
- **One complete surface, local and cloud**: `PageIndexLocalClient(storage_path=...)` is the same client as cloud — submit, tree, page content, chat, and agent tools all present in both modes, so code moves between them unchanged.
- **Cloud documents, your own model**: `api_key` decides where your documents live; a configured chat model decides who answers — and the two combine. `PageIndexClient(api_key="pi-...", chat_model="openai/gpt-5.2")` runs the same in-process document-QA engine over the live cloud tool set. Page content flows through your process to your provider on your credentials; `doc_id` targets at the prompt level; `enable_citations` stays with the managed chat.
- **Agent integration**: the cloud MCP tool contract, in-process — `client.agent_tools()` (plain functions), `as_openai_tools()`, `as_anthropic_tools()`, `as_claude_mcp()`, plus one-call `openai_agent_config()` / `anthropic_runner_config()` / `claude_agent_config()` bundles and `agent_instructions()` for the system prompt. Security and accuracy fixes from a full audit, and Claude Desktop installs again.

**Python 3.11 to 3.14 is now required.** Python 3.10 reached end of life on
2026-10-01, and the Pillow 13.0.0 security release (28 advisories, no 12.x
backport) needs 3.11. Python 3.15 is not supported yet because the Google Ads
client library declares `< 3.15`. If your default Python is outside the range,
the launcher and `install.ps1` now pick a supported one on their own, or you
can set `CLAUDE_SEO_PYTHON`; `/seo setup` then rebuilds the runtime once.

### Install or update

```
/plugin marketplace add AgriciDaniel/claude-seo
/plugin install claude-seo@agricidaniel-claude-seo
/plugin install seo-cockpit@agricidaniel-claude-seo   # optional, needs Claude Code 2.1.287+
```

Already installed? `claude plugin update claude-seo@agricidaniel-claude-seo` (auto-update is off by default for third-party marketplaces). If you use seo-cockpit, update it too: it now installs from its own branch, which is what lets Claude Desktop load claude-seo again (#344).

### Added

- **Server stack CVE exposure check** in `seo-technical` (Security category).
  A read-only detection pass that flags a site running a server-side stack with
  a known critical CVE, so the owner can patch or take it offline. Reads the
  stack from the normal response for the audited URL (`X-Powered-By`, PHP
  session cookie, WordPress signals, static/Node markers); it never fuzzes or
  sends exploit payloads, and asks whether the user owns the site before
  requesting any other path. Ships the current PHP critical-RCE advisory
  (CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619, CVSS v4.0 9.2, fixed in PHP 8.5.12 /
  8.4.27 / 8.3.36 / 8.2.35; no upstream release for 8.1 and older), the
  php.net interim mitigations, detection signals, and reporting bands in
  `skills/seo-technical/references/stack-cve-exposure.md`, with sources
  (php.net, both GitHub advisories, UK NCSC). A version string below the fixed

## New features

- **Docs:** Support persistent heading collapse and enable outlines by default in modern mode.
- **Slides (Pro):** Add dedicated picture and chart formatting tabs, with image cropping, sizing, and positioning controls.
- **Collaboration (Pro):** Add conflict callbacks with access to unsynced edits, pending-write status, and retry events.

## Improvements and fixes

- **Formulas:** Correct behavior in `ISBLANK`, `AVERAGE`, `UNIQUE`, and `PROPER`, and improve numeric literal parsing.
- **Sheets:** Fix IME input and formula permission checks during autofill.
- **Images:** Preserve aspect ratios on insertion and keep drawing anchors stable when hiding rows or columns.
- **Docs:** Improve outline navigation, table layout, and popup positioning.
- **Docs (Pro):** Improve collaborative table editing, undo/redo, and embedded content loading.
- **Slides (Pro):** Improve thumbnail rendering and scrolling performance.
- **Charts (Pro):** Improve axis and legend layout, label placement, and rendering during resizing.
- **Collaboration (Pro):** Improve automatic retries, offline edit persistence, and status notifications.
- **PDFs (Pro):** Fix missing fonts and images in imported documents.

## English

### Summary
- Update build, CI, and Docker Node.js to 24.22.1 for the October 21 security release.
- Upgrade vulnerable application and build dependencies, including Markdown rendering, sanitization, MCP, Vite, and the desktop runtime.
- Electron 44.9.3 still embeds Node.js 24.22.0. The desktop app therefore remains pending an upstream Electron release containing the October 21 Node.js fixes.

### Highlights
- Rebuild container images with patched Node.js in both build and runtime stages.
- Resolve all npm advisories reported for the main workspace and the standalone website lockfiles on October 22, 2026. This audit does not cover vulnerabilities in Electron's embedded Node.js runtime.

### Product Updates
#### Desktop
- Upgrade Electron from 41.10.7 to 44.9.3 and update the model-request HTTP client.
#### Web and Extension
- Update DOMPurify and markdown-it used for rendered content.
#### Core/Infra
- Update MCP SDK, Vite, Vitest, and vulnerable transitive packages. Update the website's separate dependency lockfile as well.
- Require Node.js 24.22.1 or a newer Node.js 24 patch for development and builds.

### Fixes
- Remove vulnerable legacy desktop download dependencies by using the current Electron downloader in electron-builder.
- Upgrade dependencies affected by proxy address parsing, command quoting, selector parsing, archive pattern handling, and MCP advisories.

### Breaking Changes / Upgrade Notes
- No user-data migration is required.
- Self-hosted Docker users must pull the new image and recreate their containers; updating Node.js on the host does not update an existing container.
- Desktop users should install this maintenance release for the available Electron and dependency fixes, but must not treat it as a complete fix for the October 21 Node.js vulnerabilities. Follow-up desktop remediation requires an upstream Electron release with those patches.

## Move older OpenWork installs to OpenCode v2 in the background

- **Older installs move to OpenCode v2 in the background.** Existing installs still using OpenCode v1 are moved over automatically, with a backup made first so your chats are kept. Windows installers also carry less duplicate engine data, and Windows can identify OpenWork's signed app files.
- **Computer use is more capable and predictable.** For Mac users, the agent can script apps directly and keeps working while you use your computer; Take over and Stop return control, and Continue resumes the task. Workbot can also script supported desktop apps. Browser pages keep a steady desktop, tablet, or phone size while the panel changes, and forms take fewer steps. When available, you can dictate into OpenWork or Workbot.
- **Chat can work with more of your existing tasks and connections.** Type `#` to add another task as context, ask the agent to create or move sidebar groups, and find connected actions with everyday wording. You can finish or repair an API-key connection in chat without sharing the key with the agent, and OpenWork Cloud tools work again in older desktop versions.
- **Documents and first launches are more dependable.** Closing an edited document now gives clear save, discard, or cancel choices, and reloading or reopening it preserves your editing session and unsaved work. Workbot can open a requested document beside chat, explain why a file could not open, and show or rebuild a computer that will not connect. Fresh desktop installs can load built-in tools even if the package registry is unavailable; slow Windows sign-in and first launch no longer hide recovery options.

## What's Changed
* Security: exclude litellm 1.107.0, which was published to PyPI with a credential stealer and backdoor, from every `litellm` requirement (the `litellm`, `entity_resolution_llm` and `all` extras, and the examples). The locked version stays 1.96.2, which is unaffected by @georgeh0 in https://github.com/cocoindex-io/cocoindex/pull/2576
* Preview works on real pipelines and writes nothing
  * Preview now handles target states under a container (rows in a Postgres / Qdrant / LanceDB table, and so on), so it no longer stops at once on most pipelines. A preview no longer stores, deletes or refreshes memos and no longer writes committed state, so it can't make the next real update skip work. Connector authors: `TargetActionSink.from_fn(fn, child_handler=...)` / `from_async_fn(...)` replace `from_fn_with_children` / `from_async_fn_with_children`, which now raise `DeprecationWarning` and don't support preview. Neo4j, FalkorDB and SurrealDB `ConnectionFactory` keep one connection per event loop and gain `close()` (neo4j, falkordb). FalkorDB now requires `falkordb>=1.6.0` by @badmonster0 in https://github.com/cocoindex-io/cocoindex/pull/2510
* feat(engine): `max_inflight_components` now bounds every running component. A parent lends its slot to one child at a time, so wide fan-outs stay within the limit and a hierarchy of any depth can't deadlock by @georgeh0 in https://github.com/cocoindex-io/cocoindex/pull/2486
* feat(core): `coco.logic_propagated_to_callers(fn)` makes a callback's logic count toward its callers' memos, even when it is called through a library function that uses `logic_tracking="self"`. Editing the callback now invalidates those memos by @georgeh0 in https://github.com/cocoindex-io/cocoindex/pull/2483 and https://github.com/cocoindex-io/cocoindex/pull/2529 (`coco.logic_tracked` remains as a deprecated alias)
* feat(code): Nix syntax support for splitting and structural code patterns by @mulatta in https://github.com/cocoindex-io/cocoi

body:
This release retunes brainstorming after its rebuild in v7.0.0. Many of you told us, rightly, that the new default questions got annoying fast and felt formulaic. Brainstorming now digs for context before it asks anything, and tries to ask better questions. We expect to keep tuning it, but we think it's better than it was.

It also trims three long skills so they better survive compaction on Claude Code, and changes the issue and PR templates to ask for a summary written by a human.

### Brainstorming

- **It digs for context first.** In an existing project, or when you point it at a spec, plan, or files, it reads them before its first message and doesn't ask what they already answer. (#2560)
- **It tries to ask better questions.** v7.0.0 opened every session the same way: an offer to skip the questions, then a generic question about "the moment you wished this existed." Now, when you've already said what you want, it plays your request back with what it found in the project and asks about the one thing still open. Later questions build on your answers and on what it found, and say what the answer would change. (#2560, #2571)
- **It offers to skip the questions only when it started on its own.** If you asked for brainstorming by name or with `/brainstorming`, it no longer offers to skip it. (#2560)
- **It lays out the approaches and writes a design doc before building.** It presents two or three ways to build the thing, recommends one, and asks you to pick. Then it writes a design doc, a short one for a small change, and builds nothing until you approve it. Some of you saw it skip the doc and start building; in one of our test scenarios, it skipped the doc without asking in 24 of 24 runs before this change and 3 of 24 after. (#2571)

Thanks to @mbcrawfo for opening #2530, and to @katyatitkova, @ertra, @blorenz, @Biomaj, @fsalum, @technicalpickles, @orochi235, @alexxburg, @fcavalieri, @CelesteCunha, and @zzzzz9999 for the reports, transcripts, and testing there.

## 🧰 WebMCP

New [page.webmcp()](https://playwright.dev/java/docs/api/class-page#page-webmcp) and [frame.webmcp()](https://playwright.dev/java/docs/api/class-frame#frame-webmcp) give access to the tools that a page registers through
the experimental [WebMCP](https://playwright.dev/java/docs/api/class-webmcp) browser API, so you can test them like
any other part of your app:

```java
Browser browser = chromium.launch(new BrowserType.LaunchOptions()
    .setArgs(Arrays.asList("--enable-features=WebMCP")));
Page page = browser.newPage();
page.navigate("https://example.com");

for (WebMCPTool tool : page.webmcp().tools())
  System.out.println(tool.name + ": " + tool.description);

Object result = page.webmcp().callTool("add", Map.of("a", 2, "b", 40));
System.out.println(result); // {content=[{type=text, text=42}]}
```

[Playwright MCP](https://playwright.dev/java/docs/getting-started-mcp) also supports WebMCP by default, with page-defined tools offered to the agent as `webmcp_<tool>`. Pass `--no-webmcp` to opt out.

[`playwright-cli`](https://playwright.dev/java/docs/getting-started-cli) exposes them as well:

```bash
playwright-cli webmcp-list
playwright-cli webmcp-call search_catalog --params '{"query":"cats"}'
```

## 🎬 Better videos

Videos can now be recorded at a custom frame rate, and the decorations for actions are styled with plain CSS:

```java
page.screencast().start(new Screencast.StartOptions()
    .setPath(Paths.get("video.webm"))
    .setSize(1920, 1080)
    .setFps(60));
page.screencast().showActions(new Screencast.ShowActionsOptions()
    .setStyle(new ScreencastActionStyle()
        .setPoint("width: 20px; height: 20px; border-radius: 50%; background: red")
        .setHighlight("outline: 2px solid #333; background: rgba(0, 128, 255, .15)")
        .setTitle("font-size: 16px")));
```

- New [`recordVideoFps`](https://playwright.dev/java/docs/api/class-browser#browser-new-context-option-record-video-fps) optio

Same-day follow-up to 0.1.17: 12 commits (10 non-merge), no new external pull
requests. It ships the fixes made on main after 0.1.17 — `mcp>=1.30` so the
HTTP MCP transport reclaims sessions, connect-time checks for custom model
endpoints (including fake-IP proxy hosts), grounding of `run_dir/…` refs and
signed amounts, Beijing codes in correlation, the macOS timeout fix and the
sdist contents — together with a leaner agent runtime: tool schemas load on
demand through `load_tools`, oversized tool results stay readable in the run
directory, Swarm sizes its context by the model window, and usage accounting
covers compaction, cancelled responses and failed streams. On the 0.1.17
pre-release verification prompt (DeepSeek V4 Pro, a 20/60 SMA backtest on
AAPL.US) a run took 7 model calls instead of 12 and 152K input tokens instead
of 706K, and reported the same figures.

### Known issues

- A retried provider error (a connection reset or rate limit) can halt live
  model decisions until the next UTC day, and a research goal's final answer
  that crosses its token budget is discarded. Both are fixed on main (see
  Unreleased) and ship with the next release.

### Changed

- Reduce agent request overhead with on-demand tool schemas while keeping the
  complete tool catalog and existing execution permissions. Ordinary backtests
  no longer request extra attribution automatically. Automatic summary titles
  remain available after the first chat exchange.
- Preserve oversized tool results in readable run artifacts and stop Swarm from
  clearing new observations before the model sees them. Context pressure uses
  the model window and includes tool schemas.
- **README credits cover every cycle again**: contributor lines for the
  0.1.13, 0.1.15, 0.1.16 and 0.1.17 cycles in all seven READMEs, each PR
  attribution checked against GitHub. The data-tools list counts the 29
  read-only data tools the MCP server serves (it said 22). The 0.1.13 notes
  below credit ModelScope (#1011)

and MCP, and saved paper accounts through `vibe-trading paper`,

completed daily bars without ever reaching a broker; saved accounts move

that cannot be computed now says so instead of turning into a plausible
number. A profit factor with no losing trade, an undefined correlation, a
factor benchmark with too few IC observations, an upside at a zero price and
an unbounded ratio come back as `null` or a refusal rather than 0; a missing
price no longer bridges a return pair, a VaR transition or a lag pair; an
after-close SEC filing no longer reaches the IC a bar early; and a misspelled

## 100,000 stars. Thank you! ⭐🐳

Orca just crossed **100,000 stars on GitHub**! Every bug report, pull request, shared workflow and recommendation has helped us get here. Thank you for building with Orca and helping shape what comes next. ❤️

To celebrate, this release brings a more capable phone experience, more dependable agent conversations, and fixes that keep your work moving across desktops and remote machines.

## The short version

- **More done from your phone:** Create and edit notes, save Markdown on headless hosts, follow relative file links, and see embedded images. Buffered terminal drafts can now survive workspace navigation, too.
- **Chats you can come back to:** Codex chats reopen correctly after undo, Claude keeps its rewound context across Orca rollbacks, and screenshots stay with the conversation. Codex’s skill picker now reflects the skills Codex actually loaded.
- **Your work stays protected:** Discard pauses autosave of the same file across workspaces. Read-only Markdown and CSV views protect your unsaved edits, and new, unstaged Markdown documents open straight into the rich editor.
- **Voice beyond the desktop:** Phone dictation works again through headless `orca serve` hosts, with a CLI command to configure the host’s OpenAI key.
- **Smoother remote work:** Reconnect hidden terminal tabs after a restart, keep browser logins when hosts pair again, and search SSH configurations with thousands of hosts without freezing the interface.
- **Small details, better flow:** Phone tabs follow desktop order, landscape layouts show the session title, keyboard controls keep their height, and worktree safety sweeps skip unchanged workspaces.

**Phone updates:** Updating Orca on the computer serving your phone also updates the phone’s served interface. Persistent terminal drafts additionally require an updated mobile shell.

This release makes the inspector's browser profiles safe when several runs go at once ([#157](https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill/issues/157), [#158](https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill/pull/158), [#159](https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill/pull/159)). The rules of `design-taste-frontend` are unchanged; only `scripts/lib/cdp.mjs` changed.

- **Fix: one inspector run could delete the browser profile of another run that was still going.** Chrome keeps no `lockfile` on macOS and Linux, so the sweep added in 2.1.0 judged a profile unused by its age alone. A second run started during a long one could then pull that run's profile away. Thanks to @t4sh for the report and the fix.
- **Leftover profiles are cleaned up again, safely.** Every profile now carries `taste-skill-owner.json` with the machine and the process IDs of the run and its Chrome. A later run removes a profile left by a killed run only when that file names this machine and neither process is alive. A profile without the file is never touched.

Profiles left by earlier versions are not removed automatically. To clear them, delete the `ad-chrome-*` folders in your temp folder (or in `TASTE_SKILL_TMP`).

Update:

```bash
npx skills add https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill --skill "design-taste-frontend"
```

Claude Code plugin users: `/plugin update`.
name: tasteskill v2.1.4

# Smart memory search by default

Memory recall now defaults to Smart: search the compact index, inspect context around relevant results, then fetch only the selected details. The agent reasons about relevance between these three steps. Local, cloud/Pro, and standalone-server instructions describe the tools available in that runtime.

The optional one-call lookup is now `dumb_search`. Its description is explicit: “Doesn’t reason about the results. Fast, but shallow. Use Smart for reliable recall.” It performs deterministic title matching and does not reason about relevance.

## Migration

- Use the `mem-search` skill for default Smart recall. Local tools are `search` → `timeline` → `get_observations`; Cloud/Pro starts with `memory_search` and can fetch selected summaries with `get_summaries`.
- Replace calls to the old `mem_search` guided/auto API and `flash_search` with the Smart workflow, or explicitly choose `dumb_search` for a shallow lookup. Auto/guided modes and continuation cursors are removed.
- Refresh existing MCP connections so clients load the new tool catalog and descriptions.

## Correctness

- Cloud timeline supports context anchored to a selected search result.
- Standalone-server recall stays scoped to its configured server project rather than reading a local worker's memory.
- Selected-detail output reports its bounds honestly and preserves selected record identities when long content must be shortened.
- Native memory lookup uses observation-only indexes, and mixed local indexes retain session/prompt ID prefixes so follow-up reads cannot select a different record kind with the same number.
- Installer prompts, public documentation, integration instructions, and generated memory guidance use the same Smart-first policy.

## Other changes since v14.0.1

- Added Hermes Agent memory support and installation, including safe handling of existing YAML configuration.
- Added fallback between an Anthropic API key and the Claude subscription, with quota cla

## CloakBrowser Pro: Stable advances to Chromium 155.0.8059.39.1 (all platforms)

Chromium `155.0.8059.39.1` is now Stable on **Linux** (x64 and ARM64), **Windows** (x64), and **macOS** (Apple Silicon and Intel).

With a valid CloakBrowser key, the wrapper automatically selects the Stable build for your platform. No version pin is required.

### What's new

- **The newest Chromium, 155**, on every platform.
- **Windows and macOS catch up with Linux:** safer proxy handling, the more patient license connection with the `--license-route` flag, and the refined Windows persona.
- **Closer to real Chrome everywhere:** graphics checks, canvas exports, network timing, the reported CPU architecture on ARM hosts, and a few more Windows font names all behave the way real Chrome does on real hardware.
- **DNS that follows your proxy:** with `--fingerprint-transparent-proxy`, sites are resolved with Cloudflare's DNS over HTTPS, sent through your proxy. Use your own with `--fingerprint-transparent-proxy-dns=<url>`, or `local` for the old behavior.
- **Clear license errors everywhere**, a **more stable macOS persona**, **quieter Windows security logs**, and a **smaller Linux download**.

Your profiles, cookies, and seeds are untouched. Only the browser itself is replaced.

### Current wrapper: v0.6.3

Update the wrapper before launching:

```bash
pip install -U cloakbrowser
npm update cloakbrowser
dotnet add package CloakBrowser --version 0.6.3
```

### Roll back if needed

If a workload regresses, pin the previous Stable build for your platform:

```bash
export CLOAKBROWSER_VERSION=154.0.8037.57.2   # Linux
export CLOAKBROWSER_VERSION=154.0.8037.57.1   # Windows, macOS
```

Remove the pin to return to the newest Stable build.

**If you hit a regression, please tell us.** [Open an issue](https://github.com/CloakHQ/CloakBrowser/issues) or email support@cloakbrowser.dev with the site and what you saw. Pinning the old build gets you unblocked; a report gets it fixed for everyone.

## [19.12.1] - 2026-10-20 - "Direct Installer Release Identity"

> The catalog stays at **2,724 skills**. This patch fixes the direct installer failing against any release published from the pre-built candidate tarball.

### Fixed

- **Direct installer `--release` installs no longer fail with "invalid registry response".** Since 19.10.0 the release pipeline publishes the pre-built candidate tarball, and `npm publish <file>.tgz` does not record `gitHead` in the registry metadata, so the installer's release-identity lookup received an empty response. The candidate packer now records the release commit in the packed manifest the way `npm publish` from a Git checkout does, so `agentic-awesome-skills --release X.Y.Z` installs again from 19.12.1 on.
- **A release without `gitHead` names the missing field** instead of blaming the registry, and points at the issue tracker. Releases published before this patch (19.10.1, 19.11.0, 19.12.0) stay as they are; use `--tag vX.Y.Z` only if you accept an unverifiable ref.

### Review scope

The packer was exercised end-to-end on a fixture: it records the release commit, keeps the artifact name `package.tgz`, restores `package.json` byte-for-byte, and fails closed on modified or untracked source. The absence of `gitHead` for a pre-built tarball was reproduced against a local registry stub, and the reverse (a directory publish records it) was reproduced as well. No live npm publication or host configuration was changed by this patch.
name: v19.12.1

# Microsoft Agent Framework for Go v0.2.0

**Embeddings, vector search, and memory for Go agents.**

v0.2.0 introduces provider-independent embedding generation and vector storage, making it easier to build retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and agents that recall relevant conversations across sessions. Start with an in-memory store, or connect to Azure AI Search or Azure Cosmos DB using the same core vector-data contracts.

## Embeddings with consistent Go APIs

The new [embedding package](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-framework-go/tree/main/embedding) provides:

- **Typed generation contracts** with ordered batch results, numeric and binary vector representations, JSON serialization, model metadata, and token usage.
- **Convenience helpers** for generating a single embedding, retrieving its vector, and pairing batch inputs with their generated embeddings.
- **Request-level configuration** for model selection, vector dimensions, and provider-specific options.
- **Built-in OpenAI and Microsoft Foundry generators** that produce float32 embeddings.
- **Opt-in OpenTelemetry instrumentation** for embedding spans, operation duration, and input-token metrics. Raw inputs and vectors are never captured by the wrapper.

See [OpenAI embeddings](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-framework-go/blob/main/provider/openaiprovider/embedding.go), [Foundry embeddings](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-framework-go/blob/main/provider/foundryprovider/embedding.go), and [embedding telemetry](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-framework-go/blob/main/provider/otelprovider/embedding.go). Added in [#1292](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-framework-go/pull/1292).

## Vector stores: local and Azure-backed

The new [vectordata package](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-framework-go/tree/main/vectordata) introduces shared contracts for typed and dynamic collections, record schemas, CRUD operations, batch helpers, portable filters, and vector search. Hybrid keyword

- **Critique and audit desktop apps.** Start an Electron, NW.js, CEF or WebView2 app with a debugging port and `impeccable detect --cdp 9222` scans the window you have open, as it stands, and leaves it exactly as it found it. Critique and audit know the recipe.

- **Fewer false alarms on real pages.** Labels that look like buttons, card numbers, code samples that scroll, text behind curtain footers and pass-through overlays, light copy on a dark halo, and frosted glass now read the way a visitor sees them. Border accents are judged per selector, not by how many blank lines sit nearby.

### Changes

- **Intraday paper trading** — a fund can rebalance on minute bars (`rebalance: minute`) inside a New York trading window, from 04:00 to 20:00. `aihf paper run <name>` stays up and advances one bar per interval; `aihf paper stop <name>` stops it after the bar in flight. Each bar is its own ledger record at `ledger/<date>/<HHMMSS>.json`, with a daily checkpoint so replay does not walk every bar. The shortest interval is 1 second, down from 10.

A patch release in two halves. **The security model now does what the docs said it did:** skills and agents get only the tools they need, the permission file ships rules that hold even in bypass mode, and every job posting is checked for hidden instructions before anything reads it. **And contributors closed fifty-eight bugs in two weeks**, most of them found by running the real tools against real data. Seventy-one entries.

## Highlights

### Least-privilege skills, agents and permissions (#642, #654)
A public review by an AI agent read the shipped configuration and concluded that local use was unsafe as configured. It had a point. The job-application skill's frontmatter granted bare `Bash`, `Edit` and `Write`. The scraper pre-approved `bun run` on any CLI path. And the `/apply` reviewer and the `/rank` scorers ran as general-purpose agents with every tool while they held untrusted posting text. Now:
- **Skill frontmatter grants nothing beyond what `settings.json` already allows.** The security guard checks every skill and command frontmatter against an exact allowlist, and a portal skill may grant only its own CLI.
- **`settings.json` ships `deny` rules that hold in every permission mode.** They block uploads via `curl`/`wget`, `scp`, `ssh`, `nc`, and reads of `.env` and credential folders. `ask` rules cover edits to the permission files themselves and `git push`.
- **The agents that read postings can read, fetch and search, but not edit or write.** These are `posting-fetcher`, `posting-scorer` and `application-reviewer`. The guard now requires every agent definition to declare its tools.
- **The 403 retry is `tools/fetch_page.py`, not a documented `curl`.** It makes one GET, checks robots.txt first, and has no upload path.

`SECURITY.md` now lists every shipped grant, its lifetime and its guard in one table, and says plainly what the permission layer does not do.

### Every posting passes an integrity gate (#654)

### Summary
- Add desktop model network settings for environments where company model endpoints require direct connections while other models need a proxy.
- Choose system, direct, or manual HTTP proxy routing and configure domain bypass rules under Model Manager → Network Settings.

### Highlights
- Apply one network configuration to model requests in the desktop instance, including model discovery, connection tests, prompt optimization, and text and image generation.

### Product Updates
#### Desktop
- Add Network Settings to Model Manager, with system routing as the default.
- Support unauthenticated HTTP proxies in manual mode. System mode resolves system proxy and PAC rules for each target address.
- Save settings on the local machine and apply them after restarting the desktop app. Restarting from the settings window is blocked while model requests are running.
- Scope these settings to model requests. Application updates and cloud backups retain their existing network configuration.

#### Web
- No functional changes.

#### Extension
- No functional changes.

#### Core/Infra
- Remove duplicate language-switching links from the README.

### Fixes
- Allow company model endpoints to avoid an unsuitable system proxy through direct mode or domain bypass rules, addressing model discovery and connection failures (#364).

### Breaking Changes / Upgrade Notes
- No user-data migration is required. Existing model configurations remain available, and system routing remains the default until settings are changed.

body:
- **Unified** SDK: vectorless RAG. **Local** or **cloud**. Index or chat.
- **Faster**: trees are created from layout stats.
- **Cheaper** than **vector index**: LLMs only write node summaries.
- Runs on your **Claude subscription**.

Index, to chat, to agent integration, one client.
Local mode needs no server, no vector DB, no PageIndex API key.

```python
client = PageIndexClient()
client.submit_document("report.pdf")
client.chat("What does the report conclude?")
```

## Highlights

- **Flash engine**: the local default (`mode="standard"` keeps the classic LLM pipeline). Embedded bookmarks are consumed when trustworthy, and tree optimization is on by default — `optimize="merge"` for the deterministic LLM-free pass, `"full"` (default) adds LLM expand, which runs a wave of nodes concurrently instead of one round-trip at a time.
- **One complete surface, local and cloud**: `PageIndexLocalClient(storage_path=...)` is the same client as cloud — submit, tree, page content, chat, and agent tools all present in both modes, so code moves between them unchanged.
- **Cloud documents, your own model**: `api_key` decides where your documents live; a configured chat model decides who answers — and the two combine. `PageIndexClient(api_key="pi-...", chat_model="openai/gpt-5.2")` runs the same in-process document-QA engine over the live cloud tool set. Page content flows through your process to your provider on your credentials; `doc_id` targets at the prompt level; `enable_citations` stays with the managed chat.
- **Agent integration**: the cloud MCP tool contract, in-process — `client.agent_tools()` (plain functions), `as_openai_tools()`, `as_anthropic_tools()`, `as_claude_mcp()`, plus one-call `openai_agent_config()` / `anthropic_runner_config()` / `claude_agent_config()` bundles and `agent_instructions()` for the system prompt. Cloud clients get the live server tool set over the MCP bridge (read-only endpoint by default); local clients get the in-process subset with the same

## Archify v3.2.0

Create a conclusion-first one-page answer from Markdown, with cited sources, interactive diagrams and browser exports.

### Added

- **One-page answers (explainer) (#993).** Ask your agent to answer as a page and Archify builds a conclusion-first explainer from a Markdown draft. Each panel answers one question, using prose, tables, steps, checklists, charts, code and validated native diagrams.
  - **Authoring and delivery:** `finalize explainer` validates, delivers atomically and checks the page. Charts come from a Mermaid fence or a CSV/JSON file next to the draft. Repository excerpts are read from the pinned commit. `patch explainer` replaces one panel by ID.
  - **Reading:**
    - Steps sit beside the diagram they walk through, and you can step through them.
    - Text and diagram nodes highlight each other.
    - Clicking a node opens the full Viewer focused on it.
    - Citations and source-linked nodes open source cards.
    - Each panel or selected passage produces a follow-up question that targets that panel.
  - **Sharing:** the page ships in four styles (clean, editorial, product, Swiss) with light and dark themes, and exports a PNG, WebP or JPG long image or prints to PDF.
  - **Examples:** four live pages in `docs/cases/explainer/`.
  - **Credit:** the one-page document direction of #942 by @goatliamia shaped this work.
  - **Acknowledgment:** thanks to @QingYunA for the early one-page diagram-and-explanation proposal and demo prototype.

### Fixed

- **Explainer pages no longer carry local paths.** The draft embedded in a page names its source and data files relative to the page, so a shared page does not reveal the author's directories. `patch explainer` resolves them against the page again.

- **Explainer long images keep the page's style and theme.** A PNG, WebP or JPG export of a dark page, or of the editorial, product or Swiss style, came out in the light clean style, because the page is drawn inside an SVG where its `<html>` is

- **Unified** SDK: vectorless RAG. **Local** or **cloud**. Index or chat.
- **Faster**: trees are derived from layout stats.
- **Cheaper than Vector Index**: LLMs only write node summaries.
- Runs on your **Claude subscription**.

Index, to chat, to agent integration, one client.
Local mode needs no server, no vector DB, no PageIndex API key.

```python
client = PageIndexClient()
client.submit_document("report.pdf")
client.chat("What does the report conclude?")
```

## Highlights

- **Flash engine**: the local default (`mode="standard"` keeps the classic LLM pipeline). Embedded bookmarks are consumed when trustworthy, and tree optimization is on by default — `optimize="merge"` for the deterministic LLM-free pass, `"full"` (default) adds LLM expand, which runs a wave of nodes concurrently instead of one round-trip at a time.
- **One complete surface, local and cloud**: `PageIndexLocalClient(storage_path=...)` is the same client as cloud — submit, tree, page content, chat, and agent tools all present in both modes, so code moves between them unchanged.
- **Cloud documents, your own model**: `api_key` decides where your documents live; a configured chat model decides who answers — and the two combine. `PageIndexClient(api_key="pi-...", chat_model="openai/gpt-5.2")` runs the same in-process document-QA engine over the live cloud tool set. Page content flows through your process to your provider on your credentials; `doc_id` targets at the prompt level; `enable_citations` stays with the managed chat.
- **Agent integration**: the cloud MCP tool contract, in-process — `client.agent_tools()` (plain functions), `as_openai_tools()`, `as_anthropic_tools()`, `as_claude_mcp()`, plus one-call `openai_agent_config()` / `anthropic_runner_config()` / `claude_agent_config()` bundles and `agent_instructions()` for the system prompt. > [!NOTE]

## 🚀 New Stuff and quality of life changes

- **A much more capable MCP server for AI agents that can solve almost any CAPTCHA** (Check the [docs](https://scrapling.readthedocs.io/en/latest/ai/mcp-server.html)):

    - **Complete browser workflows**: fill forms, click, hover, scroll, use the keyboard, handle dialogs, and wait for results in one ordered sequence. Supports different field types and slower interactions, with actions stopping at the first error.
    - **Read and search the current page without reloading it**: extract HTML, Markdown, or text from a whole page or one element. Searchable page snapshots show element roles, names, and positions, with focused views that retain the surrounding context.
    - **Run custom JavaScript and take focused screenshots**: execute scripts, including async work, with access to the page's own JavaScript. Capture individual elements, the viewport, or the full page as PNG or JPEG.
    - **Inspect network activity and reuse logins**: examine recorded requests and responses, save and restore browser login state, and interact with elements inside open or closed Shadow DOM. Read recorded traffic before closing the session.
    - **Use fewer tokens and get clearer errors**: leaner tool descriptions and shared guidance reduce repeated text, while browser and request failures reach agents with useful error messages.

- **See the requests behind the page**. Enable `record_requests=True` to record completed traffic across loads, actions, and tabs, then inspect saved responses without sending requests again.

## Claude-Mem 14.0.0: My Work and TeamBrain

### My Work: see what you asked for, and where it stands
Claude-Mem now opens on **My Work**, a local, human-readable view of the requests you've given your agents.

- **Cards, List and Agents views.** Full-width request cards with the title, a plain-language summary, who worked on it and the project. Switch to a sortable list or a view by agent. "Attention first" sorting brings anything that needs you to the top.
- **Readable summaries.** Each request gets a short everyday-language summary of what happened and the next step, written by the model you've already configured. The last good summary stays visible while a new one is written. With no compatible provider, you see the recorded wording.
- **Live status.** In progress, Needs you, No recent update, Ready to check and Checked update as work is recorded, without the page jumping while you read.
- **Review.** Mark a result as checked yourself, so an agent reporting "done" is never mistaken for a person confirming it.
- **Drill down.** Open any request to see the work behind it: workstreams, recorded evidence and the original request.

My Work is free, open source and runs on your machine.

### TeamBrain: shared work for teams (optional)
TeamBrain brings the work your team chooses to share into the same experience: open work, useful context and handoffs, without anyone's private work being broadcast. Teams can set it up self-serve at **$50 per seat per month** at https://cmem.ai/teambrain.

### Also in this release
- Codex: skips next-message suggestion and rollout-consolidation helper prompts (#4812).
- Windows tests now spawn the running Bun directly (#4814).

**Upgrade:** `npx claude-mem@latest install`

Patch release: fixes from an audit of the issue history. Most of them stop a tool from losing, overwriting or rewriting content while it reports success.

## Installation and startup

- **Skill-only installations create projects in your working folder again** (703aa72f, #144). Since v6.3.0, `project_manager.py init` placed projects relative to the installed skill. For an `npx skills` or plugin installation, that meant `.agents/projects/` or the plugin cache, where an update can replace them. Inside a repository checkout nothing changes.
- On Windows, a `python3` that never starts (the WindowsApps stub exits 9009 with no output) is no longer treated as an integrity-guard failure; the agent retries with `python` first (e1b58732, follow-up on #142).

## Source conversion and import

- **PDF**: removed four table rewrites that were written against one sample paper. They re-derived variable categories from hard-coded symbols, replaced headers, dropped rows and invented a correlation column. Extracted cells are now kept as extracted (3aa2ec62).
- **HTML**: pages are decoded by BOM and their charset declaration instead of forced UTF-8, so a `<meta charset="gbk">` page no longer comes out as replacement characters. A guessed encoding is reported (34d88c1a).
- **Web**: pages with the same title in one batch get `Report.md`, `Report_2.md` instead of overwriting each other (e847939c). A raw `.md` URL whose code fence shows `<body>` stays Markdown instead of being reduced to the example (6a92c1fd).
- **import-sources**: `.txt` sources in GB18030 or other non-UTF-8 encodings are decoded instead of replaced (39b470fe). Markdown with the same text but different companion images (`<stem>_files/`) is no longer treated as a duplicate and deleted (104bc3c9).
- **PPTX import**: `b="true"` / `i="true"` now import as bold and italic, as `"1"` already did (8bdf440c). Page-type classification matches whole words, so "Qatar" or "Department" no longer reads as a Q&A or chapter page (c0ce2420

## huashu-design 3.0：三个方向更敢，项目之间也不再长一个样

3.0 重做了「三个方向」这一步，补上了一套越用越懂你的机制。我们拿固定题目做了三轮改前改后盲选，这一版在两道上一轮输掉的题上都赢了。

### 三个方向怎么来

- **先出六个候选，再挑三个做成真稿。** 三套逻辑（最佳设计师 / 现实参照 / 秒数轮盘）各出两个候选，先画成一页缩略图，挑最强、彼此最不一样、不撞你最近项目的三版做完整设计。另外三张作为备选一起给你，看中哪张再做。
- **现实参照改成同媒介、先截图。** 做 App 找获奖 App，做 deck 找出版物和提案。新增 `scripts/ref_board.py`，把参考作品截成参考板，agent 亲眼看过再拆网格、字号比和色彩比例；截出来一片纯色（WebGL 站点常见）会被判为「没看到」。
- **加选项，不加禁令。** 暖纸衬线、深底单点缀这类外观家族不再被劝退，只在三版挤在同一家族、或和你最近的项目撞了时提醒。

### 风格库 60 → 84 种，每种都有样张

- 新增 **App 12 种**（硬件面板、液态玻璃、玩味 3D、专业相机工具……）和 **中文与东亚 12 种**（吕敬人书籍设计、宋刻本版式、民国书衣、上海摩登、香港街招、杉浦康平、田中一光、服部一成、佐藤可士和……）。
- 84 种风格每种配一张 1200×750 样张（`assets/style-specimens/`，html 源码 + jpg），每个分区一张总览图。agent 先看到风格做到位是什么样，再动手。

### 越用越懂你

- `scripts/learn.py`：开工前带出你说过的品味原话和过去的教训，收工时记下值得记的（会先告诉你）。
- **外观账本**：每次交付记一笔长什么样，下个项目主动避开。
- `scripts/design_lint.py`：只量事实的设计体检——裂图、字太小、对比度不够、控制台报错是红灯；顺手的模板装饰是黄灯；`compare` 查三版是不是换皮，`ledger check` 查和最近的项目撞没撞。
- 这些记录只在你本机的 `~/.huashu-design/`，不上传、不随 skill 分发。

### 其他

- App 原型改成有构图的展示板，不再默认一排等大的手机。
- SKILL.md 改成路由，网页 / deck / 信息图 / 动画各有模块手册，按需读取。
- 修复 #56：PPTX 导出时 svg 旁的裸文字被丢掉，现在导出后会自动比对文字。

### 怎么更新

```
git -C <你的 huashu-design 目录> pull --ff-only
```

用 `npx skills add alchaincyf/huashu-design` 安装的，重新运行一次即可。新脚本需要 Python 版 Playwright 和 Pillow：`pip install playwright pillow && python3 -m playwright install chromium`（没有时相关检查会跳过并提示，不影响出设计）。

body:
This release improves Cloud monitoring and build-cache reliability, adds deployment
automation and isolated pull-request previews, and makes workers and schedulers
easier to configure, observe and recover. These notes cover all merged changes
since 0.9.2.

### Deployment automation and previews

- **Move command variables into Environment** — review literal environment
  assignments in install, build and start commands, then migrate them into
  encrypted project or service settings. Conflicts and concurrent edits stop the
  migration before partial changes are saved. Import and saved settings share the
  same parser and guidance.
- **Prepare framework output automatically** — Next.js standalone monorepos and
  Nuxt builds retain their required workspace dependencies, public/static assets
  and selected Node or Bun runtime. Managed direct-server defaults start from the
  configured app directory; explicit custom commands retain their working directory.
- **Review older manual cache mounts** — detect duplicate package/framework cache
  mounts and offer configuration migration only after a successful build proves
  managed cache support for those paths. Existing volume data is retained. Build
  logs report observed cache reuse and build-time comparisons.
- **Catch setup problems earlier** — pre-install checks identify missing app roots
  and environment examples; command-variable, standalone startup and duplicate-mount
  guidance explains what needs attention without exposing variable values.
- **Opt into GitHub pull-request previews** — same-repository, non-draft pull
  requests can deploy their exact commit into a separate preview environment with
  preview-only variables, isolated volumes and per-service URLs. Production
  variables are not copied. Forks and unsafe shared-storage configurations are
  excluded.
- **Recover preview lifecycle operations** — durable coordination handles repeated
  webhooks, controller restarts and retryable close/merge cleanup. Optional

[中文](#cn-v0.2.1-rc.1-community) | [English](#en-v0.2.1-rc.1-community) 作为 `0.2.1` 系列的首个候选版本，本版本汇总了自 `v0.2.0-rc.2` 以来的主要用户和开发者相关变更。

新增功能

- 允许用户从“自定义插件索引源”中发现和安装插件。 @turtle1999 - 插件管理页新增「让 Agent 创建插件」入口，可保留草稿进入创造模式；发送需求后才开始执行。 @ZiyaZhang - 支持插件启用、停用、卸载及更新后的依赖同步；启用热重载时，更新或重新安装的可替换插件直接生效，无法热重载时提示重启。 @imccyu, @turtle1999 - 可选插件支持极简模式，Official 插件列表支持按需安装与当前发布版对应的 Claude Code 和 Codex 组合包，并可用于 headless、SDK 和 ACP profile。 @tianyicui, @turtle2099 - 新增实验性插件的 Session 状态记录接口，供插件写入和读取自己的会话记录。 @tianyicui - 新增实验性 Claude Code Mods 兼容层。目前阶段的主要目的是验证 Claude Code Mods API 功能大致为 DeepSeek Harness 插件的一个子集，而非为用户提供实际的完整兼容性。 @tianyicui - 新增实验性开发者工具组合包，提供会话原始日志、聊天分组与正文的双向定位，以及内嵌 NodeJS 调试工具；内嵌 DevTools 目前使用英文界面。 @imccyu, @turtle2099 - 新增实验性思考过程机器翻译插件，可在插件页启用，选择 Bing、Google 或付费 DeepSeek Flash。 @tianyicui, @ZiyaZhang, @imccyu - 新增实验性 Git Worktrees 插件，可在插件页启用，由 Agent 创建并进入独立的 Git checkout。 @tianyicui, @turtle2099 - 自定义模型 API 支持通过UI中配置各模型的推理等级，无需手动修改配置文件。 @LegGasai - pi-ai 路由支持按模型能力处理会话中的系统提示词更新，以及工具的动态新增和移除。 @Tuyixiang - 极简模式支持读取图片和自动压缩长对话，Web 与桌面端可通过 /compact 指令手动压缩上下文。 @LogosVeritas - 全局指令支持读取共享 agents 目录中的 AGENTS.md，可通过 DSH_AGENTS_HOME 指定目录。 @tianyicui - 新增 working_directory 工具，并为 TypeScript/Python SDK 提供会话工作目录的读取和切换接口。 @tianyicui - SSH 新增独立可执行的 helper 运行时，支持远端文件操作、进程、终端、沙箱和 Node PTC。 @LegGasai - Web 版支持在本机 HTTP 访问时登录 DeepSeek 账号。 @lsdsjy - 支持识别已发送消息中的密钥和令牌，并默认脱敏按需查看。 @ZiyaZhang - 新会话支持预填未发送的提示；恢复草稿或切换工作区时保留文件、目录和会话引用。 @imccyu - 新增工作步骤收起时机设置，可选择回答结束后收起，或在下一条普通消息到来时收起。 @imccyu - Markdown 文件预览将 YAML 头部元数据显示为清晰的字段列表。 @turtle2099 ### 体验优化 - 改善自动化任务详情在窄窗口中的布局，关联会话入口会按可用空间收起为图标。 @turtle2099 - 子智能体可通过配置选用独立 Agent Preset 预设，统一设置角色和工具； @grllll, @Dudu-0223 - 改进子智能体的委派与等待指引：达到委派层数上限时提前提示，等待子任务期间不再消耗新的目标执行轮次。 @ZiyaZhang, @turtle1999 - 组合包详情页显示代码来源和当前版本，便于查看安装来源及重装所需的信息。 @turtle1999 - 插件安装结果显示实际安装版本；因新版本冷却策略安装较旧版本时，提供说明和精确版本安装方式。 @turtle2099 - 工具调用在准备阶段即可显示已到达的命令说明、文件路径和内容生成进度。 @imccyu - Shell 和插件安装详情支持横向查看及复制完整命令；后台 Bash 调用可展开输
